title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: A wave of folder deletions is taken up in one pass
summary: Yesterday's replay ran once per deleted folder, and each run re reads the whole index. A wave of deletions therefore read it a second time from end to end.

highlights.title: Half the freeze on a wave of deletions
highlights.description: Two hundred deletions on a fifty thousand file index cost 853 ms and now cost 464 ms. Membership is decided by walking a path up to its parents.

sections.heading: Corrected
bullets: The note published with version 1.42.113 claimed folder deletion had gone from 406 ms to 0.1 ms. That measurement used an empty index and left out the pass that dominates.
The honest figure: reading the whole index remains, at 0.2 ms per deletion on a five thousand file project. What 1.42.113 removed was a pass whose cost had no ceiling.
